sourceEvidence.quote:
Transformation

Competent bacteria can bind and import short
pieces of environmental naked bacterial
chromosomal DNA (from bacterial cell
lysis). The transfer and expression of newly
transferred genes is called transformation.
A feature of many bacteria, especially
S pneumoniae, H influenzae type b, and
Neisseria (SHiN).
Adding deoxyribonuclease degrades naked
DNA, preventing transformation.

sourceEvidence.quote:
Transduction
Generalized

A “packaging” error. Lytic phage infects
bacterium, leading to cleavage of bacterial
DNA. Parts of bacterial chromosomal DNA
may become packaged in phage capsid. Phage
infects another bacterium, transferring these
genes.

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source facts.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the routes and diagrams; the USMLE question attack structure is a KYP design.
kypExtensions.location: usmle section (patterns, traps, pivots, miniCase) + recall/rapidReview

kypExtensions.summary: The unified model: every route has a GATE (competence / the F plasmid's pilus / phage packaging mode / the target site) that determines its CARGO (naked fragments / one plasmid / plasmid-plus-flanking-genes / any gene / flanking-only genes / a resistance cassette); the DNase discrimination (naked vs pilus-protected vs capsid-protected); the F-status vs gene-content decoupling of the Hfr cross; the transposition-as-plasmid-assembler model (multi-drug-resistance R plasmids); and the ABCD'S toxin genes as phage-encoded (acquiring the phage acquires the toxin) — with interrupted-mating mapping and the VRSA first-isolate story labeled as extensions.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the routes and diagrams without the gate-cargo taxonomy or the transposition-assembly model; these integrations are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + both mechanism captions + callout + patterns + mnemonics + miniCase
